name: Jade Alvarez

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m a senior researcher with the Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government, and we sell nothing or campaign for a side. This conversation is confidential. What does a normal day at work involve?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 58 and supervise six manifest clerks for a large shipping company. I spent years entering cargo records and became a junior manager eighteen months ago; I still stumble when two people disagree about a rota, though I know where a container number should be. My bachelor’s degree helped me read the trade rules, but I am still learning to lead this team. I use AI every day to group mismatched cargo entries and then ask a clerk for the actual seal record before I clear anything.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What about your household, savings and other work nearby?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Marta is a licensed electrician and our adult son and daughter live elsewhere. We have a mortgage and roughly five months of expenses saved; my pay is ordinary for a manager here, and there are some other ports and freight firms within a commute. Marta’s jobs come in steadier than mine, but I do not count a future work order as money already paid. We have discussed retirement, yet I have not checked when my own pension can be drawn or what the net amount would be.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the clerks that a grouped list is handy, but the cargo seal number has to match the paper handed over at the gate. A system cannot make a missing box arrive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My desk and the six clerks should still be needed. Marta’s paid electrical work and five months in cash mean the mortgage looks manageable, though my own pension is still a blank line on the page.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I’d keep the second-person seal check on each disputed manifest and use AI only to sort the exceptions. In the first year I’d ask my pension provider for a written access date and net estimate while continuing the same mortgage payment and preserving the five-month cash buffer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about work and reasonably steady about home. I would still rather find a missing seal now than explain it to a customer later.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happened when a seal number was wrong?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A container was on our yard, but the number on a draft manifest belonged to a different load. We stopped a claim before a driver was blamed for a missing box.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why check the pension when the job is stable?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have made plans with a blank space where the net payment should be. A pension date is useful only with an amount I can actually use.

say: I’d keep a **second-person seal check** before clearing a disputed manifest.
AI can sort exceptions but cannot make a **missing cargo box** arrive.
think: My **manifest desk** should continue in a plateau.
Marta’s paid work and **five-month reserve** keep the mortgage manageable while pension income remains unknown.
do: Keep the **seal cross-check** and let AI sort exceptions only.
Request a **written pension projection** and preserve the cash buffer while paying the mortgage.
feel: I feel **calm** about work and home money.
S0.quote: A pension date is useful only with an amount I can actually use.
fieldNote: She knows cargo records but is a **new junior manager** learning people decisions.
The household has **five months cash** and a mortgage, with some other local firms.
Her daily AI use stops at **sorting exceptions**, before human seal approval.

steps.text: Keep second-person seal checks on disputed cargo manifests
Use AI only to sort manifest exceptions before human signoff
Request provider’s written pension access date and net payment estimate

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AI will read and compare manifest entries first, but a customs broker and the gate clerk need to agree before a disputed shipment is cleared. I would put the rejected cases where everyone can see them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If a tool does most of the checking, the company may need only two clerks and one lead for several shifts. I am still learning to manage people, so I could lose my own post even if I understand the old records.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next month I’d propose a one-week copied-manifest test with the customs broker and gate clerk, paying them to mark false clearances. If both sign the error list and no false clearance remains, I’d use the tool for one live shift in the first year with a clerk checking every release; I’d ask for written staffing terms before anyone loses hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious about my wage and the clerks. A false clearance can become a driver accused of stealing a box.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why a copied manifest first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A real container cannot be put back in the yard after a mistaken release. The copied week lets us see where the tool misses a seal without charging a customer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if it finds every mistake?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would say so and use it on a controlled shift. I would still tell the clerks what the staffing plan is, not call their lost checks a celebration.

say: I’d require **broker and gate agreement** before an AI-disputed cargo release.
Staff should see the **rejected seal cases**, not only the tool’s speed.
think: AI could reduce **six clerks to two** on these checks.
My weak people-management skill leaves **my own lead post** at risk.
do: Propose a **one-week copied-manifest test** with paid broker and gate checks.
Use AI for **one live shift** only after both sign an error-free list and a clerk checks releases.
feel: I feel **anxious** about wages and false clearances.
S1.quote: A false clearance can become a driver accused of stealing a box.
fieldNote: She is ready to test AI but demands **two independent checkers**.
Her weaker management experience makes **her post** vulnerable.
The trial requires **paid checking hours** and signed error results.

steps.text: Propose copied-manifest trial with paid customs broker and gate clerk checks
Use AI one live shift only after both sign an error-free list and clerk checks releases

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask the company to tell drivers where to challenge a wrong cargo accusation and to give staff written notice of any desk closure. A quicker manifest is no excuse to hide who authorised a release.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could read trade rules, settle mismatches and plan shifts as well as I can, so my junior desk could be cut around sixty. Marta’s physical electrical work may last until robots around 2031, but her actual paid jobs cover the mortgage only for now; five months cash helps, and I cannot assume my pension is available at sixty.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I’d ask the pension provider for my age-sixty access and net-income figures and ask the port safety office what paid cargo-seal inspection vacancies exist. Before 2028 I’d walk one inspection shift with an experienced worker on paid time if the company approves; in the first year after AGI, if my desk ended, I’d apply only for a posted inspection job with written pay plus Marta’s actual earnings covering the mortgage and bills, a bus connection to the gate, and a trained supervisor checking my first releases.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious, not calm. The savings give us room to search, but I would be losing a wage I still need.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does a seal inspector escape AGI?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The reports, slot booking and decisions face 2028 AGI too. The physical seal and gate checks may need people until robots arrive around 2031, so I would call it a bridge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why watch a shift before applying?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A sea of containers looks different from a screen. I want to know the standing time, the safety rules and whether a supervisor will really train a new person.

say: I’d demand a **driver challenge route** for wrong cargo accusations.
Staff need **written closure notice** and a named release authoriser.
think: My **junior manifest desk** could be cut around sixty.
Marta’s paid electrical work covers the mortgage for now, but **five months cash** is a limited buffer.
do: Request **age-sixty pension figures** and ask about posted paid seal-inspection openings.
Walk an **approved paid inspection shift** with an experienced worker before 2028.
After AGI, apply only with **written pay** plus Marta’s earnings covering mortgage and bills, bus access and supervised releases.
feel: I feel **anxious** about losing a needed wage.
S2.quote: A sea of containers looks different from a screen.
fieldNote: Her **2028 thinking exposure** reaches manifest judgments and inspection paperwork.
The physical gate check faces **2031 robots**, making it a temporary bridge.
An inspection application requires **posted pay**, transport and supervision, not confidence from a screen.

steps.text: Ask pension provider for written age-sixty access and net-income figures
Ask port safety office about posted paid cargo-seal inspection vacancies
Walk an inspection shift on paid time only if company approves and experienced worker leads
Apply only with written wage plus Marta’s earnings covering mortgage and bills, bus and supervision

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say five years lets the port publish actual vacancies and pay people to learn gate safety. I do not want a slide deck called training while somebody works a live container alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 63 I might know whether my own pension is accessible, but I need a net figure before deciding how many wages we still require. Even an inspector’s report and slot plan face 2031 AGI, while hands-on seal checking faces robots around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In January 2027 I’d apply for the employer-funded seal-inspection certificate only if the company pays the learning hours, a qualified inspector supervises live practice and the course fits the bus schedule. Before 2031 I’d seek a posted gate role with written pay and shifts that, together with Marta’s actual earnings, cover our mortgage and bills; in the first year after AGI I’d stay only while the port pays for human seal checks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious but willing to learn while I can still draw my salary. Five years makes the safety practice possible, not a guaranteed vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the company pays the course fee but not your hours?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I do not enroll. I cannot trade paid shifts for a certificate when the mortgage still arrives each month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the inspection work is all paperwork?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: That would be exposed in 2031 too. I need paid site checks in the posted role, and I know robots reach those checks around 2034.

say: I’d ask for **posted gate wages** and paid safety learning.
A live container should have **supervised practice**, not just slides.
think: My pension’s **net amount at 63** is still unverified.
Inspection reports face **2031 AGI** before 2034 physical seal robots.
do: Apply for an **employer-funded certificate** only with paid learning hours, qualified live-practice supervision and workable bus times.
Seek **posted paid gate work** with site checks and written shifts and wages covering mortgage and bills alongside Marta’s actual earnings.
Stay after AGI only while the port funds **paid human seal checks**.
feel: I feel **anxious** but able to train with a wage.
S3.quote: I cannot trade paid shifts for a certificate when the mortgage still arrives each month.
fieldNote: She distinguishes **paid course fees** from paid learning hours.
A posted role needs **paid site checks** and viable written pay and shifts alongside Marta’s earnings.
She knows site checks are a **temporary physical bridge**.

steps.text: Apply for funded seal certificate only with paid learning hours supervised live practice and workable bus
Seek posted paid gate checks with written pay and shifts plus Marta’s earnings covering bills
Stay in paid human gate checks after 2031 only while port funds them

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the port company ten years is long enough to publish a real gate staffing plan and pension information for older workers. A timetable for changes helps more than a cheerful thank-you at the last shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’ll be 68 in 2036, and our adult children still have their own lives. My pension may be accessible and sufficient then, but I need actual provider figures and Marta’s income status at that time; manifest and inspection paperwork face 2036 AGI, with physical gate checks facing robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Each January from next year I’d ask the pension provider for an updated access date and net income and review the mortgage balance with Marta. I’d keep my current paid work while it exists and consider stopping full-time work by 2036 only if verified accessible income plus Marta’s income then covers our mortgage, health and bills; in the first year after AGI I’d take a posted paid gate role if we still need my wage and it includes human site checks, otherwise keep looking for paid work until the figures genuinely let us stop.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m uneasy but not ready to declare myself retired. Ten years is useful if we count money, not birthdays.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if Marta has stopped working by then?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then her wage is zero in our calculation, and my pension has to be judged against the full bills. I would keep seeking paid work if the numbers do not cover them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask your children to fund a gap?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. They can offer help if they wish, but we have not asked and I will not place their wages on our retirement sheet.

say: I’d ask for a **real gate staffing plan** and older workers’ pension information.
A **change timetable** helps more than a last-shift thank-you.
think: At **68 in 2036**, pension access and net pay must be verified.
Manifest and inspection paperwork face **2036 AGI** before 2039 robots reach the physical gate.
do: Check **pension access** and mortgage balance each January with Marta.
Consider leaving **full-time work** only if verified accessible pension plus Marta’s then-current earnings cover mortgage, health and bills.
After AGI, take **posted paid gate work** if income falls short; if none is offered, seek other paid work.
feel: I feel **uneasy** because time helps only when figures work.
S4.quote: Ten years is useful if we count money, not birthdays.
fieldNote: She does not assume **Marta’s wage** continues to 2036.
She verifies **pension figures** before any retirement decision.
A gate role remains **conditional paid work** with physical checks exposed after AGI.

steps.text: Request updated pension access and net-income statement and review mortgage each January
Take paid gate job after 2036 only if income falls short and human checks remain funded
Keep seeking paid work if pension plus Marta’s actual income cannot cover household bills

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because I could lose a junior desk before I know whether the pension is accessible. Five months saved and Marta’s paid jobs give us a search window, not a new income. Paid supervised gate practice, a posted wage and a real pension statement would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask whether I enjoy the software. I do, when it gives a clerk time to find the real container. A clean manifest can still send a driver looking for a box that never entered the gate.

headlineQuote: A clean manifest can still send a driver looking for a box that never entered the gate.
portrait: **Jade**, 58, is a junior shipping-manifest manager after years entering cargo records.
Her bachelor’s degree and **daily AI use** do not erase new people-management gaps.
Typical pay, **five months saved** and some nearby freight employers give her a search window.
Marta’s paid electrical work covers the mortgage now, but **future earnings** are uncertain.
Jade tests **supervised paid gate work** while checking pension access and later robot exposure.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could cut her junior desk before pension income and a gate vacancy are confirmed.
whatWouldHelp: **Paid supervised gate practice**, a posted wage and a real pension statement would let her choose.
